analyzed_vuln.description: In the SP-math public ECC add wrapper, `sp_ecc_proj_add_point_256` unconditionally calls `sp_256_proj_point_add_5(p, p, q, tmp)` after converting `mp_int` inputs, but does not validate that the imported projective points are well-formed/finite before entering the low-level routine. With attacker-controlled `mp_int` values (from fuzzed ECC point add inputs), this allows invalid internal state to reach `sp_256_proj_point_add_5`, which performs reads based on those assumptions and crashes with a wild read (ASan SEGV).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger path: cryptofuzz ECC_Point_Add -> `ecc_projective_add_point` (SP_MATH 256-bit path) -> `sp_ecc_proj_add_point_256` -> `sp_256_proj_point_add_5`. Input must select a 256-bit curve and provide malformed/unchecked point coordinates (and/or projective Z state) that pass harness setup but are not sanitized before SP add. The vulnerable condition is using non-safe projective add on untrusted points without pre-validation in `sp_ecc_proj_add_point_256`.
